title: French students and unions stage nationwide protests
seoTitle: Paris nationwide student and union protests

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against rising living costs, education funding issues, and public spending concerns.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand additional investment in schools, lower living costs, and action on purchasing power.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Police in Paris stated they had already made 40 arrests by 09:30 local time.

summary: Students, teachers, pensioners, and unions have staged widespread demonstrations across France, including Paris and Marseille, combining ongoing student unrest with cost-of-living and grassroots movements. The protests followed weeks of student demonstrations against classroom conditions, teacher shortages, overcrowded schools, and education funding deficits. Unions such as the CGT and the secondary school student union USL joined the movement to focus on purchasing power and public spending. Authorities anticipated hundreds of actions and marches nationwide. The government vowed to consider student complaints but noted constraints in increasing the education budget while attempting to restrain spending. In response, police deployed large-scale security measures, conducted enhanced checks, and used tear gas during clashes, making dozens of arrests.
demands: Better classroom conditions and more teachers
response: According to sources, police deployed large-scale security measures, fired tear gas in Marseille and Paris, and made 40 arrests in Paris by 09:30 local time primarily for carrying weapons or prohibited protective gear.
